newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee firms on dollar after intervention.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against the dollar and pound on Tuesday after the central bank intervened in the market on Monday, dealers said.
The rupee traded at a mean commercial rate of 20.507 for one dollar from 20.539 on Monday. The rupee firmed to a mean rate of 32.9960 against the pound from 33.0155 on Monday.

Foreign exchange dealers said the central bank sold dollars in the interbank forex market during a market intervention on Monday early afternoon. "The selling rate of the central bank was slightly below the prevailing interbank rate to maintain the rupee stable," one dealer said.

With regular market interventions by the central during the past two weeks, banks were seen able to balance forex demand and supply, thereby sustaining the rupee's exchange rate against foreign currencies.
"(Commercial) banks look to be square now with respect to their foreign exchange reserves," the dealer added.
Last week, the central bank intervened on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, selling dollars at a slightly lower rate than interbank on all three occasions.
